summary: An official list of site idents for organizations on the ARPANET, given in alphabetical order and by network address. It covers sites with present or scheduled direct connections. Scheduled sites are marked with an s and inactive addresses with an i.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists identifiers, addresses and organizations for ARPA Network sites. It marks sites that were scheduled to connect and addresses that were inactive.

subtitle: Lists official site identifiers and network addresses for ARPA Network organizations.

tldr.problem: Organizations with direct ARPA Network connections needed shared site identifiers and address information.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists sites alphabetically and by address, marking scheduled sites with s and inactive addresses with i.
tldr.outcome: RFC 384 obsoletes RFC 289 and records a historical directory dated August 1972.

today: RFC 384 obsoletes RFC 289. It is a historical list of ARPA Network sites from August 1972.

sections.title: Official Site Identifiers
sections.content:
The RFC gives official site identifiers for organizations on the ARPA Network. It includes only organizations with present or scheduled direct connections to the Network.

Scheduled sites are marked with s, and inactive addresses are marked with i. The unit metadata records that RFC 384 obsoletes RFC 289.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory lists organizations with direct ARPA Network connections or scheduled connections. Its markers distinguish scheduled sites and inactive addresses.

sections.title: Alphabetical List
sections.content:
The first list is in alphabetical order by Site Ident. It has columns for the identifier, address and organization. Some rows direct the reader to another identifier rather than repeating a full entry.

The list includes host names and TIP names, along with organizations such as universities, laboratories and agencies.
sections.plainLanguage: The alphabetical list lets a reader find a site by its identifier. Each entry provides an address and an organization name when listed.

sections.title: List by Address
sections.content:
The second list presents site identifiers in number order. This view lets a reader start from an address and find the associated site entry.

Both lists describe the same historical network directory, including scheduled sites and inactive addresses where marked.
sections.plainLanguage: The second list is organized by address instead of site name. It records the network directory as it appeared in the RFC.
